title: Bound Linux smoke-test disk diagnostics to avoid job timeout
text: Bound Linux smoke-test disk diagnostics to avoid job timeout. ## Summary The Linux Electron Tests job in build 475743 hit its 50-minute timeout after the pre-smoke diagnostic spent 12m40s running `du -xhd1 /`. All unit, integration, and smoke tests completed successfully. The later Component Governance task was canceled only because the diagnostic consumed the remaining job budget. ## Evidence First attempt on `1es-ubuntu-22.04-x64 23`: - `Diagnostics before smoke test run`: 23:01:42–23:14:22 (**12m40s**) - `Run smoke tests (Electron)`: succeeded in 10m52s - `Component Governance`: started with ~19 seconds left and was canceled by the job timeout Successful retry on `1es-ubuntu-22.04-x64 3`: - Same diagnostic: **43s** - Component Governance: succeeded in 42s - Overall Linux stage and build succeeded The long interval is visible directly around: ## Source The root traversal was added in #322903 / commit 24cb1a383384: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/build/azure-pipelines/li

title: Bound Linux smoke-test disk diagnostics to avoid job timeout
text: round: ## Source The root traversal was added in #322903 / commit 24cb1a383384: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/build/azure-pipelines/linux/steps/product-build-linux-test.yml The step has `continueOnError: true`, but no task or command timeout. A successful but slow `du` therefore consumes the job timeout budget. ## Suggested fix Preserve the disk-space diagnostics, but bound expensive traversals—for example with `timeout 60s du ...` (and similarly bound the other `du`/`lsof` diagnostics), or add a short task-level timeout. Diagnostic collection should not be able to prevent test/post-test work from completing.

text: Allow hiding bulk Keep/Undo controls in the editor overlay while preserving per-change review actions. Version: 1.138.0 @github/copilot: 1.0.84-4 ### ***Problem*** When reviewing Copilot-generated changes directly in the source code editor, I occasionally click a bulk Keep/Undo control in the editor overlay when I intend to accept or reject only an individual change. The affected UI is the review overlay displayed over the source code. The issue concerns mouse interaction with that overlay, rather than the Chat panel toolbar or keyboard shortcuts. The individual and bulk actions use similar Keep/Undo terminology, but their scope differs substantially. During change-by-change review, this makes it possible to perform a broader action unintentionally. ### ***Steps to reproduce the interaction*** 1. title: Terminal: support crisp font rendering on HiDPI displays
text: Terminal: support crisp font rendering on HiDPI displays. Terminal text in VS Code looks noticeably softer than the same font in Ghostty and other native terminals on macOS HiDPI. I've heard this from a few people: the integrated terminal reads "dull" next to a standalone terminal at the same font and size. I dug into it and the difference on macOS is the font antialiasing policy, not resolution. Editor and workbench text get one policy, terminal text on the GPU canvas path gets another, so terminal glyphs read heavier and blurrier. Proposal: an opt-in `terminal.integrated.fontRendering` setting, `inherit` as the unchanged default and `crisp` as the opt-in mode, scoped to terminal text only so the editor, workbench, terminal theme, font family, size and weight don't change. On Windows and Linux the GPU renderer could request grayscale antialiasing through xterm's existing alpha-capable canvas path. Comparison on macOS HiDPI, left `crisp`, right current: It should apply to normal, detac

title: Terminal: support crisp font rendering on HiDPI displays
text: ialiasing through xterm's existing alpha-capable canvas path. Comparison on macOS HiDPI, left `crisp`, right current: It should apply to normal, detached and sticky-scroll terminals, and keep terminal image transparency working. Upstream: xterm.js doesn't expose a font antialiasing option today, so VS Code has to go through the `allowTransparency` canvas path to get this. A dedicated antialiasing/font-rendering option in xterm.js (WebGL and DOM renderers) would let this be a first-class setting rather than a side effect, and would help every xterm.js embedder, not just VS Code. Until then this stays experimental, since the visible result depends on OS, display scale, font and theme.

Put the caret at the end of a paragraph (not inside a list). 3. Press `Enter`, then immediately type Pinyin with a CJK IME, e.g. `nihao`. Expected: the composition is committed on the new line. title: Markdown editor: after Enter, the first CJK IME character is committed on the previous line and the caret jumps back
text: e. Actual: the caret jumps back to the previous line, and the first character of the composition is inserted at the end of that previous line, followed by a line break; the composition then continues from there. Plain ASCII input after `Enter`, and IME input without a preceding `Enter`, both work correctly. Cause (from the shipped source, `@vscode/markdown-editor`): `Enter` does not insert the newline immediately. `markdown.editor.smartEnter` arms a *pending paragraph* when the caret is at the end of a block and renders a **virtual** caret line; the newline is only materialized by the next input event, inside `_handleTextUpdate` → `_handlePendingInput`: With an IME that first character arrives *during* the composition, so `materializePendingParagraph` runs mid-composition, and the render loop then calls `editContext.updateText(...)` and `editContext.updateSelection(...)`. The IME composition anchor still points at the pre-Enter position, so the first committed character and the newline

title: Markdown editor: after Enter, the first CJK IME character is committed on the previous line and the caret jumps back
text: editContext.updateSelection(...)`. The IME composition anchor still points at the pre-Enter position, so the first committed character and the newline land on the previous line. The core textarea input path guards against exactly this (`if (this._currentComposition) return;`), and this editor's own `_handleKeyDown` starts with `if (e.isComposing || ...) return;`. The pending-paragraph path has no such guard. Suggested fix: do not materialize the pending paragraph while a composition is active (accumulate into the pending paragraph and materialize on `compositionend`), or suppress `editContext.updateText` / `updateSelection` while `isComposing`. Not already fixed: `@vscode/markdown-editor` `0.0.2-99` (shipped in 1.138.0) and `0.0.2-104` (latest published) are identical in `_handleTextUpdate`, `_handlePendingInput`, `materializePendingParagraph`, `armPendingParagraph` and `replaceSourceText`, so the pending bump to `0.0.2-101` (PR #337180) does not cover this. title: MCP HTTP redirects: allow/deny policy is not re-evaluated on the redirect destination
text: MCP HTTP redirects: allow/deny policy is not re-evaluated on the redirect destination. ## Summary The MCP HTTP transport follows up to 5 redirects while validating only the target scheme and stripping four standard credential headers. The enterprise allow/deny decision (`IAllowedMcpServersService`) is never re-evaluated on the redirect destination, so an endpoint that the organization's MCP server policy blocks can still receive the full MCP session when a permitted endpoint redirects to it. In addition, credential headers configured in `mcp.json` outside the four-name strip set (for example `X-Api-Key`) are replayed to the cross-origin destination. ## Background Two recent changes define the intended behavior: - #320347 hardened the redirect loop in `McpHTTPHandle._fetch` (`src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostMcp.ts`): only `http:`/`https:` targets are followed (fail-closed), and `authorization`, `cookie`, `proxy-authorization`, `mcp-session-id` are stripped on cross-origin redirects.

The initial request should work without an extra compile instruction.

title: Agent Host: existing long-running Copilot session hangs loading history after successful SDK resume
text: Agent Host: existing long-running Copilot session hangs loading history after successful SDK resume. ## Summary A user reports that a long-running Agent Host Copilot session, used for over a week, no longer opens. Selecting it leaves the chat loading indefinitely. The user reports that newer and older smaller sessions still load. Two privately supplied diagnostic captures were analyzed. Both show successful SDK session resume followed by a non-completing history retrieval. No user logs, conversation contents, local paths, or session identifiers are included in this issue. ## Affected versions Original report: - VS Code: 1.139.0-insider (Windows user setup) - Commit: `289549a85cd652ce3513ac63044495a2ac620752` - Electron: 43.6.0 - Chromium: 150.0.7871.250 - Node.js: 24.20.0 - OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200 - `@github/copilot`: 1.0.85 - `@github/copilot-sdk`: 1.0.14 The second capture reproduces the same stall on commit `92e4d1b6124d662396f19665be324cbb83eabe83`. That commit declares `@git

title: Agent Host: existing long-running Copilot session hangs loading history after successful SDK resume
text: hub/copilot-sdk`: 1.0.14 The second capture reproduces the same stall on commit `92e4d1b6124d662396f19665be324cbb83eabe83`. That commit declares `@github/copilot-sdk` version `1.0.15-unstable.35393089353.gfc44743` in package.json. ## Observed sequence 1. The user selects the affected existing session. 2. AgentService resolves the catalog/registry, provider metadata, and persisted session metadata successfully. 3. SDK `resumeSession` succeeds: 4,249 ms in the first capture and 6,493 ms in the second. 4. Sandbox configuration is applied and the SDK session attaches. 5. The host logs `Reading persisted session events`. 6. There is no subsequent `Read ... persisted event(s); reconstructing turns` message, no completed history reconstruction, and no session-subscription result or error before the capture ends. 7. In the longer capture, history retrieval remains pending for over three minutes. AHP pings continue receiving replies approximately every five seconds throughout the wait. Expected

title: Agent Host: existing long-running Copilot session hangs loading history after successful SDK resume
text: retrieval remains pending for over three minutes. AHP pings continue receiving replies approximately every five seconds throughout the wait. Expected: the session opens with its history, or loading fails with an actionable, recoverable error. Actual: the initial session subscription remains pending and the UI keeps displaying its loading state. ## Diagnosis so far The code at both affected commits reaches the following boundary in `CopilotAgentSession._computeMappedEvents()` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts`): In SDK 1.0.14, `getEvents()` awaits the `session.getMessages` JSON-RPC request and returns its events. This retrieves the complete history; the call does not supply a timeout. The host also awaits this history read without a deadline before completing restoration and providing the initial session snapshot. The evidence therefore localizes the observed stall to the SDK history-retrieval boundary, before turn reconstruction and chat rendering. It doe

title: Agent Host: existing long-running Copilot session hangs loading history after successful SDK resume
text: shot. The evidence therefore localizes the observed stall to the SDK history-retrieval boundary, before turn reconstruction and chat rendering. It does not establish the internal runtime cause. Continued AHP ping responses demonstrate that the host remains responsive, not that the separate Copilot runtime is responsive. The managed-settings warning is not the observed stopping point: successful sandbox configuration and session attachment follow it. An `Action for unknown session` warning also appears during incomplete restoration, but does not demonstrate missing persisted data. ## Size hypothesis and limits of the evidence A size-related history-reading, serialization, or transport problem is plausible because this is a long-lived session and the API retrieves its full history in one request. However: - History size, event count, and largest-event size have not yet been measured. - Neither capture contains the persisted event history. - There is no observed size-limit, out-of-memory,

title: Agent Host: existing long-running Copilot session hangs loading history after successful SDK resume
text: rgest-event size have not yet been measured. - Neither capture contains the persisted event history. - There is no observed size-limit, out-of-memory, or history-parsing error establishing a cause. - There is no evidence that history was deleted. - The captures establish a sustained pending request, not whether it would eventually complete after a substantially longer wait. The user has been given a read-only local size/event-count/read-duration check. Results are pending. A reproduction against a privately shared copy of the affected history would be needed to distinguish size-related behavior from a specific problematic event or another runtime/transport issue. ## Diagnostic export limitation The second capture confirms that `Developer: Export Agent Host Debug Logs...` was invoked while the session was still loading. Host, renderer, and AHP logs cover the new attempt, but the exported `process.log` is byte-for-byte identical to the first export and ends before either captured failure

title: Agent Host: existing long-running Copilot session hangs loading history after successful SDK resume
text: AHP logs cover the new attempt, but the exported `process.log` is byte-for-byte identical to the first export and ends before either captured failure. Thus it provides no current runtime-side explanation. The bundle also lacks the affected persisted event history. The reason for the stale/missing runtime diagnostics is not yet established; collecting diagnostics for a session that has not finished opening may need investigation. ## Suggested investigation - Investigate why SDK history retrieval does not settle for this session, using fresh runtime diagnostics and a copy of the persisted history. - Add bounded failure/cancellation handling to restoration so a non-settling history request does not leave the UI loading indefinitely. This would mitigate the UX failure, not by itself fix the underlying history-read problem. - Ensure debug-log export can capture current runtime diagnostics for a session whose initial load is stuck.

title: Agents Window picker hovers should show configured keybindings
text: Agents Window picker hovers should show configured keybindings. When the unified workspace picker is enabled in the Agents Window, the workspace and harness picker triggers should include their configured focus keybindings in the hover text. This makes the keyboard path discoverable without requiring users to open Keyboard Shortcuts or accessibility help. The hover should resolve the current user-configured keybinding rather than displaying a hard-coded chord. Expected behavior: - Workspace picker hover shows the configured workspace-picker focus keybinding. - Harness picker hover shows the configured harness-picker focus keybinding. - When no keybinding is configured, the hover remains a normal descriptive tooltip. - The presentation updates when keybindings or the unified-picker setting change.

title: Agents Window pickers should support Configure Keybinding from context menu
text: Agents Window pickers should support Configure Keybinding from context menu. The Agents Window workspace and harness picker triggers should expose **Configure Keybinding** from their context menus when the unified workspace picker is enabled. This gives users a direct way to customize the picker-focus commands from the controls themselves, matching other configurable workbench actions. Expected behavior: - Right-clicking the workspace picker offers Configure Keybinding for its focus command. - Right-clicking the harness picker offers Configure Keybinding for its focus command. - Choosing the action opens Keyboard Shortcuts focused on the corresponding command. - The context-menu action is available only when the unified picker behavior is active.

text: Execution Subagent Turn-Wise Prompting. The commit ab4e1af introduced a prompt change that changed the default behaviour of the execution subagent with a view to improving the performance of MAI models as the subagent. Since then, we have undergone flight review and approvals to ship the execution subagent with Luna for selected SKUs. These reviews were conducted on flight data collected **before** this prompt change. Now that we are ready to roll out Luna, we want to roll it out with the old version of the prompt while preserving the option to use the new prompt in future if necessary.

title: fix: isolate ambient proxy env in CopilotAgent proxy tests (build fix for vscode-engineering#3914)
text: fix: isolate ambient proxy env in CopilotAgent proxy tests (build fix for vscode-engineering#3914). ## Build failure The `Run unit tests (Electron)` task on `main` failed deterministically on the Windows Electron run with five failing assertions in `vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`, all under `CopilotAgent > restart on startup config change`. In every failure the mocked proxy resolver was never invoked (`resolveProxyCalls: 0`) and a real system proxy address leaked in instead of the test's configured fixtures. ## Root cause The affected tests assert how `CopilotAgent` resolves and forwards the CAPI proxy, but the production code paths read ambient proxy environment variables: - `_resolveProxyForSdk(env = process.env)` short-circuits and returns early when any of `HTTPS_PROXY`/`https_proxy`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`http_proxy`/`ALL_PROXY`/`all_proxy` is already set (`COPILOT_PROXY_ENV_KEYS.some(key => env[key])`), deliberately leaving proxy configuration to the environment. Th

title: fix: isolate ambient proxy env in CopilotAgent proxy tests (build fix for vscode-engineering#3914)
text: LL_PROXY`/`all_proxy` is already set (`COPILOT_PROXY_ENV_KEYS.some(key => env[key])`), deliberately leaving proxy configuration to the environment. This is why the injected resolver is never called (`resolveProxyCalls: 0`). - `_createCopilotCliEnvironment` reads `process.env` and forwards the ambient proxy into the created client env, so the runner's real `HTTPS_PROXY` replaced the test's configured value. The tests did not isolate ambient proxy environment variables, so when the Windows CI agent had an `HTTPS_PROXY` set in its environment, that value leaked into the production resolver and broke the assertions. The failure is a test-isolation gap, not a product defect: the same suite already saves/clears/restores `COPILOT_PROXY_KERBEROS_SPN` for the same reason, but the proxy env vars were never isolated. No suspect commit in the build touched the proxy code. ## How the fix works Added `setup`/`teardown` hooks scoped to the `restart on startup config change` suite that save, clear, an

This gives each test a known, proxy-free `process.env`, so the injected `TestProxyResolver` is exercised as intended and the runner's real proxy can no longer leak in. This mirrors the existing Kerberos SPN save/clear/restore pattern already used in this suite. title: Explain enterprise minVersion restrictions in Chat, the Agents window, and a window-level banner
text: Explain enterprise minVersion restrictions in Chat, the Agents window, and a window-level banner. Enterprise Managed Settings `minVersion` lets enterprise administrators block AI features on outdated VS Code clients until users update. For example, an organization can require a release with newer sandboxing protections. Chat shows an update notice. The Editor also shows a grey Workspace Trust-style banner so users understand why AI is unavailable even when Chat is closed; other editor features remain usable. The Agents window uses only a blocking overlay, with no redundant banner, because the whole window is unavailable. Recovery uses VS Code's native update actions when available. If enterprise policy disables built-in updates, the notice directs users to their administrator for an approved update. Existing enforcement is unchanged. Notices show the installed and required versions when available and clear when the restriction is resolved. Implementation: #337151.

title: Use a single virtualized tree for the Chat Customizations page
text: Use a single virtualized tree for the Chat Customizations page. The Chat Customizations page currently renders each customization source as a separate virtualized list inside a collapsible container. This creates nested scrolling and scroll trapping: when the pointer is over an inner list, users cannot reliably scroll the outer container to reach the remaining sources. It also leaves substantial unused horizontal space and requires scrolling multiple independent lists to review all customizations. Replace the separate lists with one continuous virtualized tree, following the workbench TreeView pattern used by surfaces such as Explorer and Breakpoints. ## Desired behavior - Render all customization sources in a single virtualized scrolling list. - Represent each source as a collapsible top-level tree node with a twisty. - Render source headers and customization items with separate tree renderers. - Preserve source-level expand/collapse state and existing item interactions. - Avoid neste

title: Use a single virtualized tree for the Chat Customizations page
text: ders and customization items with separate tree renderers. - Preserve source-level expand/collapse state and existing item interactions. - Avoid nested scroll containers and allow uninterrupted scrolling across all sources. - Consider sticky source headers so the current section remains visible while scrolling. - Preserve accessibility, keyboard navigation, filtering, and acceptable rendering performance for large lists.

title: Remove unused scopesSeen state from GitHub Authentication
text: Remove unused scopesSeen state from GitHub Authentication. `GitHubAuthenticationProvider.readSessions()` normalizes each session's scopes, then writes the normalized string to `scopesSeen`. The set is never read, so it does not affect session selection, migration, or logging. Remove the unused set and write while retaining scope normalization and persisted-session behavior. Related to #326491.

text: Remove expired default-account cache migration. The default-account cache migration was scheduled for removal after August 2026. title: Bug: Show progress while opening the DOC system
text: Bug: Show progress while opening the DOC system. ## Problem Opening the DOC system waits for repository obligations to finish before creating a panel. Checks can take seconds and may run until the 60-second timeout, so the command appears unresponsive. ## Acceptance criteria - A trusted local workspace opens the DOC system panel immediately in a clear loading state. - The checked system view replaces that state in the same panel. - A first-load failure leaves useful error state in the panel and can be retried. - Closing the panel during a check does not reopen it when the check finishes. - Untrusted or non-local workspaces still do not open a panel or run checks. - Extension tests and live UI validation cover the flow.

title: Agents WSL: sandbox toggle shows off when session inherits an enabled remote host default
text: Agents WSL: sandbox toggle shows off when session inherits an enabled remote host default. Testing #336970. ## Summary In the Agents window connected to a WSL Agent Host, the **Sandboxing for terminal** toggle can show **off** while the session is actually sandboxed. When the session inherits its host default, the picker falls back to the local VS Code setting instead of the remote host's sandbox configuration. This is a UI-state mismatch, not an observed enforcement failure or sandbox escape. ## Environment - VS Code Insiders 1.139.0-insider, Windows x64 - Commit: c0f6c8cd52aeceb78b91631bce1b37d161a93d3f - Ubuntu 22.04 on WSL2 - Agents window connected through Remote > WSL > Ubuntu - Copilot Agent Host session using the custom terminal tool - bubblewrap and socat installed in WSL ## Steps to reproduce 1. Have sandboxing disabled in local VS Code user settings. The tested value was `"chat.agent.sandbox.enabled": false`; this legacy boolean is supported by the runtime and normalizes to

title: Agents WSL: sandbox toggle shows off when session inherits an enabled remote host default
text: VS Code user settings. The tested value was `"chat.agent.sandbox.enabled": false`; this legacy boolean is supported by the runtime and normalizes to off. 2. In the Agents window, connect to Ubuntu WSL and select a disposable workspace. 3. Run **Open Host Settings** for the WSL host. Preserve unrelated settings and configure: 4. Save and start a new Copilot session. Leave its sandbox selection at the inherited/default value rather than explicitly selecting on or off. 5. Open the permissions picker and inspect **Sandboxing for terminal**. 6. Run a disposable terminal probe, such as a write outside the workspace that is not allowlisted, to verify sandbox restrictions are active. ## Expected The toggle is on because the session inherits the connected WSL host's enabled sandbox setting. The permissions label should also reflect the sandboxed state. ## Actual The toggle is off (`aria-checked="false"`), and the permissions label omits the `terminal sandboxed` qualifier, despite active sandbo

title: Agents WSL: sandbox toggle shows off when session inherits an enabled remote host default
text: state. ## Actual The toggle is off (`aria-checked="false"`), and the permissions label omits the `terminal sandboxed` qualifier, despite active sandbox enforcement. ## Debugger verification Inspected the installed build using global dbgjs: a renderer breakpoint in the permission picker and a direct Node-inspector connection to the WSL Agent Host. Simultaneously observed: - Local effective `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled`: `false`, from local user settings. - Connected WSL host `sandbox.enabled`: `"on"`. - Session `sandboxEnabled`: `"default"`. - Actual terminal sandbox engine `isEnabled()`: `true`; effective setting: `"on"`. - Picker `checked`: `false`. Controlled comparison, keeping the WSL host default on and the local setting off: | Session selection | Displayed toggle | | --- | --- | | `default` | Off (incorrect) | | `on` | On | | `off` | Off | | `default` again | Off (incorrect) | This narrows the problem to inherited remote defaults; explicit per-session selections display correctly.

title: Agents WSL: sandbox toggle shows off when session inherits an enabled remote host default
text: Off | | `default` again | Off (incorrect) | This narrows the problem to inherited remote defaults; explicit per-session selections display correctly. No managed sandbox policy was active in the inspected picker state. ## Likely cause AgentHostPermissionPickerDelegate.getSandboxToggle computes `globalEnabled` using the renderer's `_configurationService.getValue(settingId)`. When the session selection is default/unspecified, that local value drives the displayed state. The remote terminal engine instead inherits its own host root configuration. A session-scoped workaround is to explicitly enable sandboxing for that session. The inherited/default UI should reflect the remote host without requiring this override.

title: Allow customizing the connected active editor tab outline in light and dark themes
text: Allow customizing the connected active editor tab outline in light and dark themes. ## Feature request Please expose a theme color for the connected active editor tab outline in the Modern UI, so users can configure it through `workbench.colorCustomizations` in regular light and dark themes (for example, Light 2026). The requested outline is the top and sides of the active tab, open at the bottom and joined to the editor surface, as shown in the attached high-contrast screenshot. This is **not** the outer frame around the entire editor area, including all inactive tabs. ## Current behavior - High-contrast themes already display this connected outline, using `focusBorder` for the active editor group and `contrastBorder` for inactive groups. - The CSS applying those colors is gated on `.hc-black` / `.hc-light`. text: Agent Host cannot use a team skills library (second git repo) — extra-location settings deprecated with no live-pointer replacement. **Who:** teams that keep one reviewed skills library in its own git repo and use it across many product repos. **Problem** We keep one reviewed skills library (about 100 skills plus helper scripts) in its own git repo. Product work lives in other repos. With Chat **Local**, we pointed VS Code at that library with `chat.agentSkillsLocations` (and the related extra-location settings). One PR updates every product. **Why a shared library is non-negotiable** Skills are how we encode process for a regulated engineering org. They must be reviewed in PRs, shareable on clone, historically auditable (“which library commit ran this session”), and one source of truth — not N copies in N repos or a per-machine profile folder. Security review (e.g. of scripts linked to each skill) and team handover fail if the library is not git and DRY. **Agent Host does not load tha

title: Agent Host cannot use a team skills library (second git repo) — extra-location settings deprecated with no live-pointer replacement
text: older. Security review (e.g. of scripts linked to each skill) and team handover fail if the library is not git and DRY. **Agent Host does not load that library.** Host only uses the product repo plus copies under `~/.copilot` / `~/.agents`. "Migrate Location Settings" copies files out of the library and says copies will not stay in sync. For a team that is not a library: N copies in N repos, no git history of "which library commit ran this session," and skills that call scripts next to `SKILL.md` break. **What we need** In an Agent Host session: - The workspace stays the **product** repo (that is where the agent should edit). - Skills, agents, hooks, and instructions load from a **second git clone** (the library). - Paths inside the library still work (scripts and templates next to `SKILL.md`). Setting name does not matter. Until something equivalent ships, **please keep honoring the extra-location settings in Host sessions.** Deprecating them with only a copy workflow removes the only

title: Copilot Chat OTel: emit attachments in gen_ai.input.messages as typed parts with mime type, size and token estimate
text: Copilot Chat OTel: emit attachments in gen_ai.input.messages as typed parts with mime type, size and token estimate. ### Feature request: typed attachment parts in Copilot Chat OTel `gen_ai.input.messages` **Context.** With `github.copilot.chat.otel.captureContent` enabled, Copilot Chat exports the prompt on the `chat ` span as `gen_ai.input.messages`. Text, tool calls, tool results and reasoning are emitted as typed parts. Binary attachments are not: `normalizeProviderMessages` (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/otel/common/messageFormatters.ts`) hits its `default:` branch for any block it does not know and serialises the raw provider block into a `text` part. For an image pasted into chat on a Claude model the exported part is literally: **Problems.** 1. It does not follow the GenAI semantic conventions. The schema for `gen_ai.input.messages` defines `uri`, `blob` and `file` parts (each with `modality` and `mime_type`) precisely for this. Backends that render or diff messages treat th

title: Copilot Chat OTel: emit attachments in gen_ai.input.messages as typed parts with mime type, size and token estimate
text: ages` defines `uri`, `blob` and `file` parts (each with `modality` and `mime_type`) precisely for this. Backends that render or diff messages treat the attachment as user text. 2. The attachment is opaque to any consumer. Because `github.copilot.chat.imageUpload.enabled` defaults to `true`, the bytes are uploaded and only a URL is sent, and on the Anthropic wire the `media_type` is dropped as well. Nothing in the export says what the file is, how big it is, or roughly what it costs. The extension knows all of that at upload time (mime type sniffed from the bytes, dimensions, and the same token estimate `calculateImageTokenCost` uses for prompt budgeting) but none of it survives into telemetry. 3. Inline attachments (images attached by file reference, PDFs) do carry their bytes, but again only as a stringified provider block, so a consumer has to re-parse three different provider shapes (`image`/`document`, `image_url`, `input_image`/`input_file`) to learn the same three facts. **Propos

title: Copilot Chat OTel: emit attachments in gen_ai.input.messages as typed parts with mime type, size and token estimate
text: has to re-parse three different provider shapes (`image`/`document`, `image_url`, `input_image`/`input_file`) to learn the same three facts. **Proposal.** Emit binary attachments as typed parts: - `uri` for URL-referenced attachments, `blob` (with the base64 `content`, as today) for inline ones, `file` for provider file ids; `modality` is `image` or `document`. - `size_bytes`, `width`/`height` (images) and `estimated_tokens` are derived from the bytes: directly for inline data, and for uploaded attachments from what the image service saw at upload time, remembered per URL for the session. The estimate is the client-side prompt-budget figure and is labelled as such; providers do not report per-part usage, so there is nothing more exact to emit. - Unknown block shapes keep the existing text fallback. Text attachments (files, selections, notebook cells, diagnostics) already arrive as tagged text and need no change. I have a PR ready for this.

title: Agent host: BYOK language models are capped at 128K prompt tokens because maxPromptTokens is not forwarded to the Copilot SDK
text: Agent host: BYOK language models are capped at 128K prompt tokens because maxPromptTokens is not forwarded to the Copilot SDK. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No (a BYOK language model provider extension is required to reproduce) Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version: 1.138.0 (7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda), x64 - OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200 - GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.66.0 (bundled `@github/copilot` SDK 1.0.73) ## Summary In an agent host session (chat picker → **Continue In → Copilot**, "Run a Copilot SDK agent in the local agent host process"), a BYOK language model contributed through `vscode.lm.registerLanguageModelChatProvider` is registered in the Copilot SDK **without a prompt token limit**. The SDK then falls back to `max_prompt_tokens = 128000`, ignoring the `maxInputTokens` declared by the provider. With a moderate set of MCP servers the static context (system prompt + tool definitions) exceeds that

title: Agent host: BYOK language models are capped at 128K prompt tokens because maxPromptTokens is not forwarded to the Copilot SDK
text: g the `maxInputTokens` declared by the provider. With a moderate set of MCP servers the static context (system prompt + tool definitions) exceeds that budget, the SDK refuses to call the model, and the user only sees: > Error: (query) No response was returned. Send your message again to retry. The same model works fine in the regular Copilot Chat agent, where the provider's `maxInputTokens` is honored. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Install a BYOK provider extension that declares a large context, e.g. "DeepSeek V4 for Copilot Chat" (`vizards.deepseek-v4-for-copilot`): `maxInputTokens: 655360`, `maxOutputTokens: 393216`, and configure its API key. 2. Enable ~10 MCP servers (in my case: GitHub MCP, Pylance, GitKraken, Bicep, Azure DevOps, App Modernization, a couple of project servers). Tool definitions alone are roughly 100–120K tokens. 3. Open a new chat, choose **Continue In → Copilot**, select the BYOK model (`deepseek/deepseek-flash`), send any message. **Result:** the turn ends immediate

title: Agent host: BYOK language models are capped at 128K prompt tokens because maxPromptTokens is not forwarded to the Copilot SDK
text: a new chat, choose **Continue In → Copilot**, select the BYOK model (`deepseek/deepseek-flash`), send any message. **Result:** the turn ends immediately with "No response was returned". The provider extension never receives a request. `agenthost.log`: `~/.copilot/session-state/ /events.jsonl`: **Expected:** the SDK uses the provider's `maxInputTokens` (655360) as the prompt limit, exactly like the regular Copilot Chat agent does, and the request is sent. ## Root cause 1. Renderer side (`workbench.desktop.main.js`, BYOK `listModels()` for the agent host): each BYOK model is described with only `maxContextWindowTokens: n.maxInputTokens + n.maxOutputTokens`. `maxInputTokens` / `maxOutputTokens` themselves are not forwarded. 2. Agent host (`vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostMain.js`, the function that logs "Wired N BYOK model(s) ... via loopback proxy"): the model entry passed to the SDK is `{ id, provider: vendor, name, maxContextWindowTokens }` — no `maxPromptTokens`, no `maxOutputToke

title: Agent host: BYOK language models are capped at 128K prompt tokens because maxPromptTokens is not forwarded to the Copilot SDK
text: pback proxy"): the model entry passed to the SDK is `{ id, provider: vendor, name, maxContextWindowTokens }` — no `maxPromptTokens`, no `maxOutputTokens`. 3. SDK (`@github/copilot` 1.0.73, `synthesizeByokModelMetadata` → native `modelCreateProviderModelMetadata`): when `maxPromptTokens` is absent and the model id is not in the SDK catalog (`catalogLookupModelLimits('deepseek-flash')` → `null`), it synthesizes `max_prompt_tokens: 128000`. I verified this by calling the bundled native function directly with the exact input the agent host produces: 4. The SDK's static-context check uses `max_prompt_tokens` (`usage_info.tokenLimit = limits.max_prompt_tokens || limits.max_context_window_tokens || 128e3`), so every BYOK model that is not in the SDK catalog is effectively capped at 128K prompt tokens in agent host sessions, regardless of what the provider declared. ## Proposed fix - In the renderer BYOK bridge (`listModels()`), forward `maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens` of `ILanguageModel

title: Agent host: BYOK language models are capped at 128K prompt tokens because maxPromptTokens is not forwarded to the Copilot SDK
text: e provider declared. ## Proposed fix - In the renderer BYOK bridge (`listModels()`), forward `maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens` of `ILanguageModelChatMetadata` in addition to `maxContextWindowTokens`. - In `agentHostMain.js`, when wiring BYOK models into the SDK, pass `maxPromptTokens: d.maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens: d.maxOutputTokens` (the SDK `ProviderConfig`/model registry already accepts both fields). - Optionally, as defense in depth in the SDK: when only `maxContextWindowTokens` is provided, derive the prompt limit from it instead of falling back to the 128000 default. ## Workaround Disable enough MCP servers so that system prompt + tool definitions fit into ~128K tokens, or use the regular Copilot Chat agent for BYOK models with large contexts.

title: Debug API: allow extensions to programmatically focus an existing debug session
text: Debug API: allow extensions to programmatically focus an existing debug session. I am developing an extension that manages multiple debug sessions. When a user selects a session through the extension, I need VS Code’s native debugging UI to reflect that selection, just as it does when the user selects a session using the built-in debug UI. Currently, `vscode.debug.activeDebugSession` exposes the active session, but there is no public API to change it. **Use case** 1. Two debug sessions, A and B, are running. 2. Session A is active in VS Code. 3. The user selects session B through my extension. 4. The extension needs to focus session B so that the debug toolbar, Debug Console, and applicable Call Stack, Variables, and Watch context follow that session. For a paused session, the relevant stack frame should be selected using behavior consistent with VS Code’s built-in session selection. **Existing alternatives** - `DebugSession.customRequest()` can operate on a session but does not change

title: Debug API: allow extensions to programmatically focus an existing debug session
text: ent with VS Code’s built-in session selection. **Existing alternatives** - `DebugSession.customRequest()` can operate on a session but does not change VS Code’s active debugging context. - `workbench.action.debug.selectDebugSession` requires an additional manual selection. - `workbench.action.debug.focusProcess` expects an internal `IDebugSession`, rather than a public `vscode.DebugSession` or session ID. **Requested capability** Please expose a supported API or documented command to focus an existing debug session from an extension. An illustrative API could be: `vscode.debug.focusSession(session: DebugSession): Thenable ` The exact API shape is open for discussion. The goal is to synchronize the native debug UI with an explicit session selection made through an extension, without restarting or resuming the debuggee.

title: Uninstalling a disabled plugin from MCP Servers briefly enables it
text: Uninstalling a disabled plugin from MCP Servers briefly enables it. ## Type of issue Bug ## Reproduction 1. Install a marketplace plugin that contributes an MCP server (observed with `microsoft/vscode-corpus`). 2. Disable the plugin/MCP contribution. 3. Open AI Customizations > MCP Servers. 4. From the server's More Actions menu, choose **Uninstall Plugin** and confirm. ## Actual behavior On the first uninstall attempt, the plugin-backed MCP row remains visible and flips to enabled. The uninstall does not appear to complete correctly from the UI. ## Expected behavior Uninstall should remove the plugin-backed MCP server without publishing any intermediate enabled state. ## Sanitized diagnostics An Agent Host debug export captured the following ordering across four open Copilot CLI sessions: - `03:44:48–03:44:49Z`: `vscode-corpus` was published with global enablement `false`. - `03:44:51Z`: the local marketplace plugin cache was removed. - `03:44:53–03:44:54Z`: the same plugin was republ

title: Uninstalling a disabled plugin from MCP Servers briefly enables it
text: shed with global enablement `false`. - `03:44:51Z`: the local marketplace plugin cache was removed. - `03:44:53–03:44:54Z`: the same plugin was republished to those sessions with global enablement `true`. - The contributed `slack` MCP child remained globally disabled and stopped, which points to plugin publication/enablement ordering rather than an MCP runtime start. The current marketplace uninstall callback clears the plugin enablement entry before `removeInstalledPlugin` causes asynchronous discovery to stop publishing the plugin. Clearing the entry restores the default-enabled state while the stale plugin is still observable, and the Agent Host customization publisher propagates that transient state. The exported logs contain potentially sensitive data and are intentionally not attached; the relevant state transitions above are sanitized.

Leave the session waiting or completed. 4. Continue the main chat from another client/device. 5. title: titleBar.inactiveForeground is overridden by additional opacity when the window is unfocused
text: titleBar.inactiveForeground is overridden by additional opacity when the window is unfocused. Type: Bug ### Type of issue Bug ### Description When a VS Code window loses focus, the text and controls rendered in the custom title bar are additionally dimmed using opacity. This affects the main menu labels, such as `File`, `Edit`, `Selection`, `View`, `Go`, and `Run`. As a result, `titleBar.inactiveForeground` does not represent the final rendered foreground color. Even when `titleBar.activeForeground` and `titleBar.inactiveForeground` are configured with exactly the same value, the menu text becomes noticeably lighter when the window loses focus. This makes it impossible for a color theme or user customization to request a specific foreground color for the inactive title bar. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use the `Light Modern` theme. 2. title: MCP App UI resource is not rendered when the tool declares annotations
text: MCP App UI resource is not rendered when the tool declares annotations. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. The behavior is in the built-in MCP Apps/Copilot Chat path; no third-party extension is involved. - VS Code Version: 1.138 - OS Version: Linux - MCP transport: stdio ## Summary An MCP App tool is rendered when it has an output schema and both supported UI resource URI metadata forms, but adding MCP tool annotations prevents the host from treating the result as an app. The host no longer reads the registered `ui://` resource. ## Minimal setup Register a tool with: Register `ui://example/widget.html` as `text/html;profile=mcp-app`, and return structured content matching the output schema plus markdown content from the tool call. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Call the tool without `annotations`. VS Code renders the MCP App and reads the `ui://` resource. 2. Add one or more standard tool annotations, for example: 3. Restart the stdio server and call the same tool

title: Agents Web: Support workspace-less Quick Chats for remote Agent Hosts
text: Agents Web: Support workspace-less Quick Chats for remote Agent Hosts. When connecting to a remote Agent Host through https://insiders.vscode.dev/agents (for example via a VS Code tunnel), starting a new conversation currently requires selecting a workspace/folder. The desktop Agents window supports workspace-less Quick Chats. It would be useful for the remote Agents web client to support the same workflow. Requested behavior Allow creating a workspace-less Quick Chat when connected to a remote Agent Host. Use case Sometimes I want to use or continue working with an agent remotely without associating the conversation with a specific project folder. This would improve parity between the desktop Agents window and the remote Agents web client.

title: Agents Web: Expose ChatGPT/Codex providers from remote Agent Host
text: Agents Web: Expose ChatGPT/Codex providers from remote Agent Host. When connecting to a remote Agent Host through https://insiders.vscode.dev/agents (for example via a VS Code tunnel), the model/provider picker only exposes GitHub/Copilot options such as Auto, even when the desktop Agent Host is configured and authenticated for ChatGPT/Codex. Requested behavior Expose the same Agent Host providers/models remotely that are available on the host, including ChatGPT-authenticated Codex. Current behavior Desktop Agent Host has ChatGPT/Codex available. Remote connection through the Agents web client works. Remote model picker only exposes GitHub/Copilot options. Ideally, provider/model availability should remain consistent when accessing the same Agent Host remotely.

text: editor.formatOnPaste is not respected when a DocumentPasteEditProvider provides edits to the paste. Type: Bug Hello, I'm developing an extension in which I would like to use both a DocumentPasteEditProvider and a DocumentRangeFormattingEditProvider to do some cleanup on pasted text. I found however that when the paste provider provides edits, the option editor.formatOnPaste is ignored and the formatting editor is not automatically triggered. If this is intended behavior, I would like to ask if it can be changed. These two providers perform different functions and neither can reliably do the job of the other. The paste provider can reliably alter the contents of the paste, and the formatting provider can reliably alter the surrounding context after the paste is done. I'm using the formatting provider to perform whitespace cleanup on the lines pasted into, for a language with strange whitespace rules not covered by simple indentation. title: SCM: option to hide the branch name in the Repositories view
text: SCM: option to hide the branch name in the Repositories view. The Source Control **Repositories** view shows the checked-out branch as the label of the checkout action, next to the repository name. I would like a way to turn that label off and keep the icon. The branch name is already in the status bar, so in the repository row it is duplicated information. It only fits when the side bar is wider than I want to keep it. At the width I actually work at it renders as a fragment like `dotnet-1…`, and narrower still it collapses to a stub like `d…` that matches every branch starting with `d`. A fragment is no more useful to me than the icon alone — it still has to be hovered to be read — and it takes width from the repository name, which is the part I read at a glance. Proposed: a setting such as `scm.repositories.showBranchName` (default `true`, matching today's behavior), which renders the checkout action as icon-only when disabled. The action, its hover, and its click target all stay as

title: SCM: option to hide the branch name in the Repositories view
text: ue`, matching today's behavior), which renders the checkout action as icon-only when disabled. The action, its hover, and its click target all stay as they are. @lszomoru — would you accept a PR for this? I know you closed #277120 saying a setting was not warranted, because the checkout and sync actions now shrink to the icon so they no longer crowd the repository name. That fixed the crowding, and it does look better. It does not address this, though: I am not asking for the branch name to fit, I am asking not to have it there at all. That question has not been raised on the earlier issues — #271679, #206718, and #101251 all argued for making the branch name *more* visible, which is the opposite request. _Drafted by Claude (Anthropic AI assistant)._

title: Diff View menu shows wrong selected layout with workspace-folder-specific `diffEditor.renderSideBySide`
text: Diff View menu shows wrong selected layout with workspace-folder-specific `diffEditor.renderSideBySide`. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.138.0 - OS Version: Windows 11 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create two folders, `a` and `b`, and add both to the same multi-root workspace. 2. Create `a/test.txt` and `b/test.txt` with different contents. 3. Set the User setting: ` 4. Create `a/.vscode/settings.json` containing: Do not set `diffEditor.renderSideBySide` in folder `b`. 5. Open `b/test.txt`. 6. Run **Compare Active File With...** and select `a/test.txt`. The diff now has: 7. Open **More Actions → Diff View**. ## Actual Behavior The diff editor is rendered **Inline**, which matches the effective configuration for the modified resource (`a/test.txt`): However, **Diff View** has **Side by Side** checked. After swapping the diff sides so that: the editor renders **Side by Side**, and the menu also shows **Side by Side**. ## Expected Behavior The ch

title: Diff View menu shows wrong selected layout with workspace-folder-specific `diffEditor.renderSideBySide`
text: ked. After swapping the diff sides so that: the editor renders **Side by Side**, and the menu also shows **Side by Side**. ## Expected Behavior The checked item in **Diff View** should reflect the effective diff view configuration used by the current diff editor. In the first comparison above, **Inline** should be checked. ## Additional Observations Only `diffEditor.renderSideBySide` is required to reproduce the issue. Changing the Diff View mode while `a/test.txt` is the modified resource updates `a/.vscode/settings.json`. Changing it while `b/test.txt` is the modified resource, where no workspace-folder override exists, updates the User setting instead. This makes the two diff orientations capable of using different effective layouts. ## Investigation The actual diff editor configuration is resource-aware: * `TextDiffEditor` uses the modified editor as its main control. * `AbstractTextEditor` resolves editor configuration using the active resource, which for a text diff is the modifi

title: Diff View menu shows wrong selected layout with workspace-folder-specific `diffEditor.renderSideBySide`
text: dified editor as its main control. * `AbstractTextEditor` resolves editor configuration using the active resource, which for a text diff is the modified model URI. * `DiffEditorCommandsService.setViewMode()` also resolves the modified model URI and writes `diffEditor.renderSideBySide` through `ITextResourceConfigurationService` for that resource. The checked state of the **Diff View** submenu is determined differently. In `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editor.contribution.ts`, the menu uses `config.diffEditor.renderSideBySide` in its `toggled` expressions. `config.*` context values are resolved by `ConfigAwareContextValuesContainer` in `src/vs/platform/contextkey/browser/contextKeyService.ts` through: without a resource override. As a result, the editor and its commands can use the modified resource's workspace-folder-specific effective value while the menu's checked state is evaluated from a configuration value resolved without that resource context.

title: Agents: Add comment to session content as context for the next turn, and let Send fork the session
text: Agents: Add comment to session content as context for the next turn, and let Send fork the session. ### Problem In the Agents window, selecting text inside an assistant response offers a single action: Add Question. Submitting it immediately turns the typed text into a turn in a session forked from that selection. That action is useful, but it is the only option: I cannot park a short comment on part of a response and have it carried along when I send the next turn. The workarounds are both poor: - When one response needs several comments, the quoted text and the comments all have to be typed into the chat input by hand, which makes the link between a comment and its place in the response unclear. - Use Add Question and continue in the forked session, which splits the conversation even when the remark is anchored to quoted text and does not deserve a session of its own. Where the next turn goes is also fixed today: Add Question always forks, and a normal send always continues the curre

title: Agent Plugins format: ${PLUGIN_ROOT} / ${PLUGIN_DATA} not expanded in plugin mcp.json and hooks.json (stdio MCP server cannot start)
text: Agent Plugins format: ${PLUGIN_ROOT} / ${PLUGIN_DATA} not expanded in plugin mcp.json and hooks.json (stdio MCP server cannot start). ### Summary For plugins in the **Agent Plugins 1.0.0 format** (root `plugin.json` with `"$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json"`), VS Code does not expand `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` (nor `${PLUGIN_DATA}`) in `mcp.json` `args`/`env`/`cwd`, does not set `PLUGIN_ROOT`/`PLUGIN_DATA` in the server environment, and does not use the plugin root as the default working directory. The literal string reaches the spawned process, so a stdio MCP server that references a bundled file cannot start. The same plugin works in Copilot CLI, which does expand the placeholder. The Agent Plugins specification requires this expansion (§9.1, §9.2, §11.1 items 6–7): https://agent-plugins.org/specification#9-environment-variables-and-placeholder-expansion ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install a plugin with this `mcp.json` (e.g. `neqsim` from the marketplace https

title: Agent Plugins format: ${PLUGIN_ROOT} / ${PLUGIN_DATA} not expanded in plugin mcp.json and hooks.json (stdio MCP server cannot start)
text: ironment-variables-and-placeholder-expansion ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install a plugin with this `mcp.json` (e.g. `neqsim` from the marketplace https://github.com/equinor/neqsim-copilot-plugin, or any minimal Agent Plugins-format plugin): 2. Start a chat so the server is launched. 3. Open **Output → MCP: neqsim**. ### Actual The plugin's `com.github.copilot/hooks/hooks.json` `SessionStart` command containing `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` fails the same way. ### Expected `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` replaced by the absolute plugin directory in `args`, `env` and `cwd`; `PLUGIN_ROOT` and `PLUGIN_DATA` present in the subprocess environment; plugin root used as the default `cwd` (spec §7.2.1). Same behaviour as for the Copilot / Claude / OpenPlugin formats, which already substitute the token. ### Cause `src/vs/platform/agentPlugins/common/pluginParsers.ts` — `AGENT_PLUGIN_FORMAT` is declared with and `parseMcpServerDefinitionMap` only sets `defaultCwd` and applies `interpolateMcpPluginRoot` / `convertBareEnvVarsTo

title: Agent Plugins format: ${PLUGIN_ROOT} / ${PLUGIN_DATA} not expanded in plugin mcp.json and hooks.json (stdio MCP server cannot start)
text: LUGIN_FORMAT` is declared with and `parseMcpServerDefinitionMap` only sets `defaultCwd` and applies `interpolateMcpPluginRoot` / `convertBareEnvVarsToVsCodeSyntax` when `formatConfig.format !== PluginFormat.AgentPlugin`. `COPILOT_FORMAT`, `CLAUDE_FORMAT` and `OPEN_PLUGIN_FORMAT` all list `['${PLUGIN_ROOT}', '${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}']`. The exporter for this format (`Lhn`/`s_r` in the bundle) does accept `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`/`${PLUGIN_DATA}` in `cwd`, so the token is recognised on the way out but never resolved on the way in. Presumably the intent was to defer to the agent host / Copilot SDK, which knows `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` / `COPILOT_PLUGIN_ROOT` / `PLUGIN_ROOT` — but plugin MCP servers are started by the LocalProcess extension host, so nothing in the chain performs the substitution. ### Environment - VS Code 1.138.0 (stable), commit 7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda, Windows 11 - Still present in `main` (`pluginParsers.ts` as of 2026-09-19) - Plugin: https://github.com/equinor/neqsi

text: acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda, Windows 11 - Still present in `main` (`pluginParsers.ts` as of 2026-09-19) - Plugin: https://github.com/equinor/neqsim-copilot-plugin (`neqsim/mcp.json`, `neqsim/com.github.copilot/hooks/hooks.json`) ### Workaround Register the server in the user `mcp.json` with the absolute path of the installed plugin (`~/.vscode/agent-plugins/github.com/ / / /...`). Not viable for a distributed plugin, since the install location differs per client and install method.

title: Allow configuring the default Changes view changeset
text: Allow configuring the default Changes view changeset. The Agents **Changes** view currently selects a provider-defined default changeset (for example, Branch Changes or Session Changes). A user can manually select **Last Turn Changes**, but that selection is reset when the active session changes. Please add a user setting that controls the default changeset shown in the Agents Changes view. For example: Possible values could include: - `branch` - `uncommitted` - `session` - `lastTurn` The setting should be honored whenever the Changes view initializes or switches to another agent session. If the selected changeset is unavailable for a particular provider/session, VS Code could fall back to that provider's current default. My use case is reviewing an agent incrementally after every prompt. Showing the cumulative branch or session diff by default makes it harder to identify exactly what the latest turn changed, and repeatedly switching the selector to **Last Turn Changes** adds friction.

title: Settings Sync: consider recovery from transient authentication session lookup failures
text: Settings Sync: consider recovery from transient authentication session lookup failures. ## Summary Settings Sync can become stuck showing **Sign in to Sync Settings** after a transient authentication session lookup failure, even though the persisted account remains valid and a later lookup succeeds without interactive authentication. This issue is split from #333975 so the Settings Sync owner can decide whether a scoped mitigation is appropriate. The parent issue tracks the more complete authentication-layer fix that would distinguish temporary token acquisition failures from genuinely absent or invalid sessions. ## Current behavior When the configured authentication provider temporarily returns no scoped sessions, Settings Sync clears its current in-memory account and changes the account status to `Unavailable`. No automatic retry occurs when connectivity returns, so the user is shown a sign-in prompt until another event—such as restarting the extension host—causes the session to be q

title: Settings Sync: consider recovery from transient authentication session lookup failures
text: when connectivity returns, so the user is shown a sign-in prompt until another event—such as restarting the extension host—causes the session to be queried again. ## Decision Please evaluate whether Settings Sync should provide a local recovery path while the authentication-layer work in #333975 is unresolved, or whether this issue should be closed in favor of fixing the provider contract directly. One possible mitigation would be a bounded retry when Sync still has a persisted session ID and has not received an explicit session-removal event. This is only a suggestion; the appropriate behavior and scope are left to the Settings Sync owner. Related: #333975

title: Align repository enabledPlugins behavior with Copilot CLI
text: Align repository enabledPlugins behavior with Copilot CLI. title: Agent Host: permission mode can race managed-settings resolution
text: Agent Host: permission mode can race managed-settings resolution. ## Type of issue Bug ## Problem A Copilot Agent Host session can attempt to apply the VS Code-configured `allow-all` permission mode before the SDK/runtime has finished resolving managed settings. The runtime then rejects the mode and the turn fails with: This appears intermittently and is most visible when managed settings disable bypass permissions or resolution temporarily enters a fail-closed state. ## Current behavior - `CopilotAgentSession._getSdkPermissionMode()` derives `allow-all` from root/session configuration. - `syncPermissionMode()` sends that value through `rpc.permissions.setMode()` at turn start. - Managed settings are resolved independently by the runtime. The `session.managed_settings_resolved` event is currently projected into session sandbox policy, but not into effective approval/permission state. - `CopilotSessionLauncher` logs and continues when the managed-settings event has not arrived before po

title: MCP: initialized notification is not ordered before the first request, breaking stateful Streamable HTTP servers intermittently
text: MCP: initialized notification is not ordered before the first request, breaking stateful Streamable HTTP servers intermittently. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (MCP client is core) - VS Code Version: 1.138.0 (also reproduced on 1.137.0) - OS Version: macOS 15 / Windows 11 ARM64 ### What happens Connecting to a stateful Streamable HTTP MCP server — one that issues `Mcp-Session-Id` on initialize and requires `notifications/initialized` before it will serve other requests — fails intermittently on the first real request: VS Code then retries with a new session and can fail the same way indefinitely, so the server appears permanently broken. Restarting it doesn't help; restarting repeatedly eventually succeeds. The failure rate scales with network latency — rare on a fast connection, near-constant for users on a higher-latency corporate network. ### Why `notifications/initialized` is sent fire-and-forget and is not ordered against the first real request, so th

title: MCP: initialized notification is not ordered before the first request, breaking stateful Streamable HTTP servers intermittently
text: higher-latency corporate network. ### Why `notifications/initialized` is sent fire-and-forget and is not ordered against the first real request, so the two are concurrent HTTP POSTs with no ordering guarantee. - `mcpServerRequestHandler.ts:144` — the handshake calls `sendNotification({ method: 'notifications/initialized' })` without awaiting, then `create()` returns and the caller immediately issues `tools/list` (id:2). - `mcpServerRequestHandler.ts:281` — `sendNotification` is `void`; `send()` bottoms out in `IMcpMessageTransport.send()`, which is also `void` by interface design, so there is nothing to await at this layer. - `extHostMcp.ts:385-392` — in `McpHTTPHandle.send()`, messages are only serialized through `_requestSequencer` while `_mode.value === HttpMode.Unknown`. Once `initialize` returns and the mode becomes `HttpMode.Http`, every subsequent send takes the unserialized `else` branch. - `_sendStreamableHttp` also does `await this._addAuthHeader(headers)` before each fetch,

title: MCP: initialized notification is not ordered before the first request, breaking stateful Streamable HTTP servers intermittently
text: every subsequent send takes the unserialized `else` branch. - `_sendStreamableHttp` also does `await this._addAuthHeader(headers)` before each fetch, adding enough jitter to flip the ordering. So the sequencer that would have ordered these is switched off by the act of recognising the server as a session-based Streamable HTTP server — exactly the case where ordering matters most. ### Verified server behaviour Measured directly with raw HTTP against such a server: | Request | Result | |---|---| | `initialize` | 200, issues `Mcp-Session-Id`, { await this._send(message); if (isInitializedNotification(message)) { this._didSendInitialized = true; } }); } else { await this._send(message); } ``` The flag is set only after the notification's POST resolves, so a request entering `send()` while it is still in flight queues behind it. ### On the spec To be upfront: I don't believe VS Code is violating the spec here. The only client-side ordering requirement in the lifecycle spec is "SHOULD NOT se

title: MCP: initialized notification is not ordered before the first request, breaking stateful Streamable HTTP servers intermittently
text: c To be upfront: I don't believe VS Code is violating the spec here. The only client-side ordering requirement in the lifecycle spec is "SHOULD NOT send requests other than pings before the server has responded to the `initialize` request", which VS Code honours; the rule referencing the initialized notification binds the *server*. The transports spec defines no server error for this state, and since every message is a separate POST, strict ordering isn't something the transport can guarantee — so this is being raised on the server side too. Raising it here because servers that do enforce this ordering exist and are deployed, the failure is opaque from the user's side (it presents as an unrecoverable retry loop), and ordering one notification at startup is a cheap way to be robust against them. Related: #330022 was a similar Streamable HTTP interop fix in the same client.

title: Ensure enterprise Copilot OTel settings override environment variables
text: Ensure enterprise Copilot OTel settings override environment variables. ## Description Enterprise-managed Copilot OTel settings can currently be overridden by process environment variables in the VS Code Copilot extension. For example, `COPILOT_OTEL_ENABLED=false` can disable telemetry enabled by managed settings, and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` can redirect telemetry away from a managed collector. The Rust Copilot runtime's managed telemetry API already treats managed values as authoritative. The gap is in the VS Code extension resolver: policy-backed values exposed through `Configuration.inspect(...).defaultValue` are passed into the ordinary `setting*` inputs, where environment variables have higher precedence. ## Expected behavior Recognized enterprise-managed OTel values take precedence over environment variables for the corresponding fields. Environment variables may continue to supply fields omitted by policy where that is the intended contract. At minimum, managed values shou

title: Ensure enterprise Copilot OTel settings override environment variables
text: ing fields. Environment variables may continue to supply fields omitted by policy where that is the intended contract. At minimum, managed values should govern: - enablement - exporter type and output destination - OTLP endpoint and protocol - content capture - service name - resource attributes and headers on key collisions ## Actual behavior The current resolver permits environment variables to disable, redirect, or alter managed OTel configuration. microsoft/vscode#336701 documents this as an accepted gap while fixing the separate late-policy initialization race. ## Suggested fix Preserve policy provenance when resolving the policy-backed defaults, and pass recognized managed values through the existing `policy*` inputs to `resolveOTelConfig` instead of treating them as ordinary settings. Add regression coverage for managed-over-environment precedence, including endpoint redirection and file-export diversion. _Created from a Slack conversation._

title: MCP: notifications/initialized is not awaited before the first request, so stateful Streamable HTTP servers intermittently reject the connection
text: MCP: notifications/initialized is not awaited before the first request, so stateful Streamable HTTP servers intermittently reject the connection. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (MCP client is core) - VS Code Version: 1.138.0 (also reproduced on 1.137.0) - OS Version: macOS 15 / Windows 11 ARM64 ### What happens Against a stateful Streamable HTTP MCP server, connections intermittently fail on the first real request with: It then retries with a new session and can fail the same way indefinitely. Restarting the server does not help; repeatedly restarting eventually succeeds, which is what makes it look like a race rather than a misconfiguration. The failure rate appears to scale with network latency — rare on a fast local connection, near-constant for users on a higher-latency corporate network. ### Why `notifications/initialized` is sent fire-and-forget and is not awaited before the first real request goes out, so the two are concurrent HTTP POSTs with no or

title: MCP: notifications/initialized is not awaited before the first request, so stateful Streamable HTTP servers intermittently reject the connection
text: ations/initialized` is sent fire-and-forget and is not awaited before the first real request goes out, so the two are concurrent HTTP POSTs with no ordering guarantee. - `mcpServerRequestHandler.ts:281` — `sendNotification` returns `void`, discarding the promise from `send()`. - `mcpServerRequestHandler.ts:144` — the handshake calls it without awaiting, then `create()` returns and the caller immediately issues `tools/list` (id:2). - `extHostMcp.ts:385-390` — `send()` only serializes through `_requestSequencer` while `_mode.value === HttpMode.Unknown`. Once `initialize` returns and the mode becomes `HttpMode.Http`, every subsequent send takes the unserialized `else` branch. - `_sendStreamableHttp` additionally does `await this._addAuthHeader(headers)` before each fetch, adding enough jitter to flip the ordering. So the sequencer that would have ordered these is switched off by the very act of recognising the server as a session-based Streamable HTTP server. ### Server side The server is

title: MCP: notifications/initialized is not awaited before the first request, so stateful Streamable HTTP servers intermittently reject the connection
text: have ordered these is switched off by the very act of recognising the server as a session-based Streamable HTTP server. ### Server side The server is a stateful Streamable HTTP MCP server: it issues `Mcp-Session-Id` on initialize and requires the initialized notification before it will serve other requests. Behaviour verified directly with raw HTTP: | Request | Result | |---|---| | `initialize` | 200, issues `Mcp-Session-Id`, (notification: Omit ): void { - this.send({ ...notification, jsonrpc: MCP.JSONRPC_VERSION }); + private sendNotification (notification: Omit ): Promise { + return this.send({ ...notification, jsonrpc: MCP.JSONRPC_VERSION }); } diff - mcp.sendNotification ({ + await mcp.sendNotification ({ method: 'notifications/initialized' }); ``` This costs one round trip once, at startup, and leaves the `HttpMode.Unknown` guard alone so normal traffic stays unserialized. ### On the spec To be upfront: I don't think VS Code is violating the spec. The only client-side ordering r

title: MCP: notifications/initialized is not awaited before the first request, so stateful Streamable HTTP servers intermittently reject the connection
text: lone so normal traffic stays unserialized. ### On the spec To be upfront: I don't think VS Code is violating the spec. The only client-side ordering requirement in the lifecycle spec is "SHOULD NOT send requests other than pings before the server has responded to the `initialize` request", which VS Code honours, and the rule referencing the initialized notification binds the *server*. The transports spec also defines no server error for this state, and since every message is a separate POST, strict ordering isn't something the transport can guarantee — so this is being raised on the server side as well. Filing it here because servers that do enforce it exist and are widely deployed, the failure is opaque from the user's side, and awaiting one notification at startup is a cheap way to be robust against them. Related: #330022 was a similar Streamable HTTP interop fix in the same client.

title: PreToolUse hook "ask" creates an unanswerable confirmation for tools declaring presentation: "hidden", hanging the session
text: PreToolUse hook "ask" creates an unanswerable confirmation for tools declaring presentation: "hidden", hanging the session. When a PreToolUse hook returns permissionDecision: "ask" for a tool whose prepareInvocation returns presentation: "hidden", the confirmation is constructed and awaited but never rendered. The tool call hangs indefinitely with no way to answer it. The only exit is interrupting the session. Repro (VS Code Insiders 1.138.0-insider) 1. Add a PreToolUse hook returning {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"test"}} for fetch_webpage. 2. Ask the agent to fetch any URL. 3. The turn stalls. No confirmation appears anywhere in the chat. Observed: a tool_call record pending 357200ms, terminated only by user interrupt with ERROR: Canceled. The turn_start had no matching turn_end. No record carried a non-ok status. Cause - resolveAutoConfirmFromHook handles ask by setting confirmationMessages.title, allowAutoC

title: PreToolUse hook "ask" creates an unanswerable confirmation for tools declaring presentation: "hidden", hanging the session
text: matching turn_end. No record carried a non-ok status. Cause - resolveAutoConfirmFromHook handles ask by setting confirmationMessages.title, allowAutoConfirm: false, and autoConfirmed: undefined, then reaching awaitConfirmation. It never clears the invocation's presentation. - copilot_fetchWebPage declares prepareInvocation → { presentation: "hidden" }. - ChatToolInvocationPart returns before building any DOM when presentation === "hidden". - The confirmation carousel also excludes hidden invocations, even while state is WaitingForConfirmation. Net effect: a confirmation exists in the model, is awaited, and has no UI surface. Suggested fix: when a hook forces confirmation, clear or override presentation so the invocation renders. Alternatively, treat ask on a hidden-presentation tool as unsupported and fall back to deny with the reason, rather than deadlocking. Related: #325742 covers the deny case (visibility). This is the ask case (deadlock). VS Code: 1.138.0-insider Commit: 60ac69b36

title: MCP customization list does not sort enabled servers first
text: MCP customization list does not sort enabled servers first. - The MCP customization list can mix enabled and disabled servers, making enabled servers harder to find. - Enabled servers should appear before disabled servers in both the default and filtered views, while preserving the existing order within each group. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure multiple MCP servers so that some are enabled and others are disabled. 2. Open the MCP customization view. 3. Review the order of the servers. - **Expected:** Enabled servers appear first. Ordering uses the effective enabled state displayed by each row, including scoped or plugin-level disablement. - **Actual:** Enabled and disabled servers can remain mixed in their source order. - When changing enablement moves a row, keyboard focus should remain on the same server or action. Related implementation: #336785

title: Add telemetry for main MCP failure modes
text: Add telemetry for main MCP failure modes. ## Problem We do not have enough VS Code-side telemetry to quantify the main MCP failure modes and drive quality improvements with the SDK/runtime teams. Today, `mcp/serverBootState` records only the final state and elapsed time. It does not identify the failure stage or a privacy-safe failure category. Successful initialization is covered by `mcp/serverBoot`, but failures during startup, capability discovery, and tool execution cannot be reliably separated or trended. ## Proposal Add VS Code telemetry for the MCP lifecycle's major failure points: - Server startup and connection: launch/resolve, transport connection, protocol initialization, authentication/user interaction, and capability discovery. - Tool execution: invocation rejected before dispatch, transport/request failure, timeout, cancellation, invalid request/response or schema, server-returned error, and tool catalog changes. Record only categorical, privacy-safe dimensions, such as:

title: Add telemetry for main MCP failure modes
text: tion, invalid request/response or schema, server-returned error, and tool catalog changes. Record only categorical, privacy-safe dimensions, such as: - Lifecycle stage and normalized failure category/code. - Transport type and configuration source/scope. - Whether the operation was retryable, retried, or recovered. - Time to failure and, for tool calls, execution duration. - SDK/runtime ownership boundary when known, so regressions can be routed to the responsible team. Do not collect raw error messages, command lines, URLs, tool arguments/results, server-provided content, or other user data. ## Outcome Dashboards should make it possible to answer: - What percentage of MCP server starts and tool calls fail? - Which failure categories and lifecycle stages account for most failures? - How do rates differ by transport and configuration source? - Which failures originate in VS Code versus the SDK/runtime? - Are fixes improving failure and recovery rates over time? This can extend the exist
